economy.summary: Busy week. The Fed held rates on Oct 28, but two officials voted for another hike. On Oct 29, Q3 GDP grew a stronger-than-expected 3.4% while September PCE inflation rose to 3.6%, so the economy is growing but prices are still running hot. Big tech earnings split: Microsoft beat, but Alphabet had its worst day since 2004 (about −13%) on a profit miss and heavy AI spending, and ServiceNow fell about 25% on slowing growth. Amazon reports Oct 29 after the close and AMD on Nov 3. The backdrop is unchanged: a war-driven oil shock keeps inflation high and the Fed leaning toward hikes, which is hard on stocks priced for fast growth.
economy.fed: The Fed raised rates in September, then held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10–2 vote; the two dissenters wanted another hike. It gave no clear signal about December.
economy.fedNext: The next meeting is Dec 8–9. On Oct 28 the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% (Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a hike) and said it wants more information before acting again. Since then, Q3 GDP grew 3.4% and September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% (core 3.1%), both on Oct 29. Markets price about one more quarter-point hike in 2026. Chair Warsh also said the Fed will hold fewer meetings starting in 2027.
economy.oil: The US–Iran war has largely shut the Strait of Hormuz since late February. Brent crude settled near $117 a barrel on Oct 23, a six-month high, as traders bet the U.S. could resume strikes on Iran; U.S. crude (WTI) was about $101 on Oct 26.

GOOGL: Q3 revenue rose 25% to about $127.6B, slightly below estimates, and Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B. But adjusted EPS of $2.12 fell far short of the roughly $3.00 expected, free cash flow was negative $9.1B, Alphabet kept its 2026 capex plan at $195B–$205B, and Other Bets lost $20.4B. The stock fell about 13% on Oct 29, its worst day since going public in 2004, wiping out roughly $500B of market value.
Alphabet heads for its biggest drop in market value (Yahoo Finance)
MSFT: Fiscal Q1 revenue rose 19% to $92.3B and adjusted EPS was $4.89, both above estimates. Azure grew 48%, beating Microsoft's own 44–45% forecast, to $33.2B; Microsoft Cloud reached $63.9B (up 30%); and the Q2 outlook calls for Azure growth of 49–50%. Capex of $45.2B came in below the roughly $50.7B expected. Shares rose about 4% after hours but slipped about 1% on Oct 29 as Alphabet's drop weighed on tech.
Azure beats Microsoft's own forecast again (Stock Titan)
AMZN: Reports Q3 today, Oct 29, after the close. Amazon guided sales to $197B–$202B (up 9–12%) and operating income to $22.5B–$26.5B; analysts expect about $202B in sales, EPS near $1.96 and AWS growth of roughly 35–38%. It raised its 2026 capital spending plan to about $220B, so free cash flow is expected to stay negative. Amazon also owns a large stake in Anthropic (analysts estimate 15–20%), which filed for its IPO on Oct 26.
META: Q3 revenue rose 26% to $64.6B and Q4 is guided to $73B–$76B. But a $9.9B legal charge (a settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental-health claims) cut operating income 37%; without it, EPS would have been $7.40 instead of $3.83. Capital spending of $34.9B was more than the business brought in, so free cash flow was negative $2.1B, and Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex range (now $135B–$145B). It also plans a non-voting Class C share, handed out as a one-for-one stock dividend in January 2027. The stock fell 7% the next day.
Meta sinks as free cash flow turns negative (CNBC)
NVDA: A market-driven week: the stock fell 4.4% on Oct 22 in the AI-spending selloff, then rose 2.4% to $216 on Oct 26 as Anthropic's IPO filing lifted chip stocks; it's about 10% below its record close of $239. Nvidia also expanded its security partnership with CrowdStrike. Next earnings: Nov 18.
HOOD: Record Q3 revenue of $1.42B (up 12%) was a bit below the roughly $1.43B expected; adjusted EPS of $0.60 beat $0.55, while GAAP EPS fell 16% to $0.51. Trading revenue rose 19%, but crypto revenue fell 55%, and prediction-market contracts ($173M) brought in more than crypto ($120M). Gold subscribers hit a record 5.2 million. The stock fell 3.3% the next day.
SOFI: Record Q3: adjusted net revenue rose 44% to $1.37B, adjusted EBITDA rose 70% to $470M, net income was $241M ($0.18 a share, up from $0.11) and members grew 35% to 17.1 million. SoFi raised its 2026 outlook to about $5.04B in adjusted net revenue and $0.61 in EPS, and gave a first 2027 outlook of about $6.4B in revenue and $0.90 in EPS. The stock rose about 18% in the two days after the report.
UNH: Q3 beat (adjusted EPS $4.69 vs. $4.15 expected) and 2026 guidance was raised to at least $20.50 per share.
TSLA: Q3 revenue was flat at $28.1B, but gross margin improved to 19.6% (from 18.0% a year ago) and adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 estimate. GAAP net income fell 43% to $787M, the operating margin was just 2.6%, energy revenue fell 16%, and free cash flow was $1.5B (vs. $4.0B a year ago). Tesla said its robotaxis have driven nearly 2 million unsupervised miles. The stock fell 3% the day after the report, then jumped 5% on Oct 26.
Q3 beat on margins and cash flow (investinglive)
NFLX: Q3 EPS of $0.87 beat the $0.82 estimate and revenue of $12.9B (up 12%) matched, with a 34.6% operating margin. But Q4 revenue guidance of $13.4B came in under the $13.5B expected, and Netflix cut its 2026 ad revenue forecast to about $2.7B from $3B, citing a slower rollout of some ad features. The stock fell 5% the next day and closed at $63.90 on Oct 26, down 32% this year.
Why Netflix fell despite the beat (Finviz)
CRWD: Rose about 15% from Oct 19 to Oct 26 as cybersecurity stocks rallied on worries about a wave of AI-enabled cyberattacks. CrowdStrike also expanded its partnership with Nvidia to build security in at the chip level, and Mizuho raised its price target to $275. The stock has more than doubled this year.
NOW: Q3 revenue of about $4.11B was roughly as expected, but adjusted EPS of $1.00 missed $1.02, subscription gross margin fell to 80% from 83%, and ServiceNow guided Q4 growth in contracted revenue (cRPO) to about 18.5%, down from 20.5%. That revived fears that AI will slow software sales, and the stock fell about 25% on Oct 29, its worst day in over 14 years. ServiceNow raised its AI contract target to $1.7B, and some analysts called the drop an overreaction.
KO: Q3 EPS of $0.91 and revenue of $13.4B beat estimates, and Coca-Cola raised its full-year outlook to about 11% earnings growth. Shares dipped anyway on slowing demand in North America, after a record close on Oct 22; the stock is up about 33% this year.
Coca-Cola pulls back on slowing U.S. demand (Schaeffer's)
BA: Q3 revenue of $24.2B came in slightly above forecasts, but the core loss of $0.34 a share was wider than analysts expected (GAAP loss: $0.26). Free cash flow was positive at $0.5B, the order backlog hit a record $745B, and Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in the quarter.
PYPL: Q3 adjusted EPS rose 8% to $1.45, well above the roughly $1.31 expected, but revenue grew only 2% to $8.6B, a bit short of forecasts. GAAP EPS fell 4% to $1.25.
NKE: Fiscal Q1 beat on profit (adjusted EPS $0.48 vs. $0.44 expected), but revenue fell 4% to $11.2B, Greater China sales fell 22%, and Nike now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to fall by a high-single-digit percentage with EPS of $1.15 to $1.35 (Wall Street had about $1.67). It also launched a $2.5B cost-savings plan.
JPM: Q3 profit rose 6% to $15.3B and revenue rose 8% to $50.2B, but adjusted EPS of $5.75 missed estimates near $5.85. Equity trading jumped 49%, buybacks were cut 84% from Q2, and the full-year net interest income outlook was raised to about $106B.
TSM: Q3 revenue of $46.7B (up 41%) beat the top of its own guidance; EPS rose 69% with a 58.7% operating margin. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to $52.3B to $54.3B (about 58% growth) and now expects 2026 revenue to grow about 44%.
ASML: Record Q3 sales of 11.7B euros with a 57.5% gross margin. ASML guided Q4 sales to 14.2B to 15.2B euros and full-year 2026 to 44B to 45B euros, saying customers raised equipment plans because of AI.
LLY: Q3 revenue of $24.4B and adjusted EPS of $7.48 beat estimates on strong demand for its GLP-1 drugs, and Lilly raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $91B–$92B. The stock rose about 6% on Oct 29.
Lilly pops on GLP-1 demand (Yahoo Finance)
VRT: Q3 revenue rose 61% to $4.31B and adjusted EPS of $2.21 beat estimates; Vertiv raised its full-year outlook. The stock jumped 16.5% on Oct 28.
Vertiv soars, GE Vernova slips (24/7 Wall St.)
GEV: Q3 revenue rose 27% to $12.64B and adjusted EPS of $4.81 beat estimates; the order backlog hit a record $197B and GE Vernova agreed to a $9B deal for Trench Group. The stock dipped about 6% at first but recovered most of the drop.
GE Vernova falls despite beat and raise (24/7 Wall St.)
